findings.claim: Half the listed kinds have no front matter and no fixed ## sections, and the plan does not say what their schema holds. kmctl new doc writes no front matter at all (docs.py new_doc writes '# title' then the skeleton); docs/README.md, a section index ('# Name', concepts.py:259) and log.md have none either, and OKF v0.2 sections 8 and 9 say index.md and log.md should carry none (okf_validate.py:353,379); the root index may carry only okf_version (okf_validate.py:365). log.md's ## headings are appended dates (append_log), so no fixed x-kmctl-sections list can match what kmctl writes, and the indexes have no ## sections, only entry lines. As written, r3's 'sections appear in the listed order' cannot hold for the log, and for the other kinds the schema would either be empty (passing r2 and r3 trivially while stating nothing) or invent fields. The plan must say per kind what the schema states: no front matter allowed (OKF 8/9), okf_version only, a dated-heading pattern for the log, an entry-line shape for indexes, or drop kinds whose shape is not a front matter plus section list.

'Built from the code so it cannot drift' only holds for SKELETONS and ALLOWED_FIELDS' names; several values the schema must state are not in src at all. The status values (draft, stable, deprecated) are defined only in the vendored test validator (tests/vendor/okf/okf_validate.py:43), not in kmctl; kmctl writes stable in concepts.py:101 and deprecated in supersede.py as literals. ALLOWED_FIELDS has no notion of required or of per-kind use (its values are citations). The manifesto's sections are inside a string literal in scaffold._files, and kmctl's own .okf/manifesto.md does not have them (it starts at 'Where knowledge lives' and has no 'What this is for'), so those are a starting skeleton, not the kind's shape. The architecture kind's type value and its '## Depicts' last section live only in a rule file (repo_rules/diagrams-stay-current.md), and no verb writes the kind, so r3 never tests it. The plan must either move these into named constants in src that the writer and the schema both read (a manifesto skeleton list, status values, per-kind required/used fields, the architecture Depicts rule), or say which parts are hand-kept and add a test that pins each one (e.g. the status enum equals the vendored STATUS_VALUES; this repo's own manifesto and architecture pages validate against their schemas).

The help text and r4 say the schema 'is what kmctl check and the strict validator expect', which is false of the code. kmctl check reads no front matter and no sections (checks.py: indexes, links, prototypes only). The strict validator checks type is non-empty, status is in its set, stale_after is a timestamp and sources items have resource; it checks no per-kind type value, required field set or section. So the schema is stricter than both checkers and enforced by neither, and an agent reading the help would trust a check that does not exist. Either the help says what is true (what kmctl writes and the rules ask for; kmctl check does not enforce it) or the plan grows to make kmctl check enforce it, which is a larger ticket.

r3 and the Done-when ask for every kind 'with and without --stale-after and --source', but the dependency new-concept-freshness refuses --source on a handoff. The row as written cannot pass; it should say every kind except handoff takes --source.

The plan gives a kind's body three forms (a fixed list of ## sections, a heading pattern, or none), but the architecture kind fits none of them: its sections are free and only the last one is fixed (## Depicts). r3 then checks this repo's .okf/architecture/overview.md (The CLI, The plugin, The action, Depicts) against that schema. A fixed list [Depicts] fails r3; a heading pattern checks each heading and cannot say Depicts comes last; none drops the one rule the table was meant to carry. The x-kmctl-sections shape needs a fourth form, such as free sections with a required last section, or the plan must say how architecture is described.

The decision kind's x-kmctl-sections is the fixed list [Context, Decision, Consequences], but kmctl decision supersede, a writer the kinds.py docstring says reads this table, appends '## Correction, DATE' sections. Any superseded record then fails its own kind's schema, although the help and docs/reference/commands.md say the schema is what kmctl writes. 8 of this repo's decisions (0001-0006, 0008, 0011) fail the decision schema for this reason. The prose description mentions the Correction section; the machine-readable form says otherwise.

entries.change: A decision's schema allows any number of dated Correction sections after its fixed list, given as x-kmctl-then; the manifesto's description says the operator may change its sections.
The Correction heading comes from the CORRECTION constant in kinds.py.
A superseded record matches the decision schema, an unknown trailing section does not, and x-kmctl-then is checked for shape.
The kmctl schema section describes x-kmctl-then and the Correction sections.
